title: How far does Punjab's line rise from its lowest month to its highest?
description: Punjab's line graph of the highest temperature of each month is read at its lowest dot and its highest dot. The two readings are taken away from each other to find the rise, which is then set beside Kerala's small rise. The video breaks Keeko's doubt that the height of the top dot is the rise.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rise is the highest reading take away the lowest reading, not the height of the top dot. Watch for students who give the highest reading as the rise.

source: Read Punjab's line: what is the rise from its lowest month t
video_script.why: The child can read one dot of a line graph but has not yet found how far a line climbs between its lowest and highest dots.
video_script.substitution: Read the lowest dot and the highest dot of Punjab's line, take the lowest reading away from the highest, and compare with Kerala's rise.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the monthly maximum temperature in Punjab and Kerala
video_script.wrong_answer: the rise is thirty eight degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the height of the top dot as the rise and forgets to take away the height where the line started.
video_script.payoff_line: the line rises by about nineteen degrees

final_answer.value: about 19 degrees, much more than Kerala's rise of about 4 degrees
final_answer.spoken: the line rises by about nineteen degrees, much more than Kerala's rise of about four degrees

maths_rules: Punjab, monthly maximum temperature in 2023: lowest about 19 degrees Celsius in January, highest about 38 degrees Celsius in June
rise = highest reading - lowest reading = 38 - 19 = 19 degrees (about)
Kerala, from the other worked video: highest about 33 in April, lowest about 29 in July, rise 33 - 29 = 4 degrees (about)
slip: 38 is the height of the top dot, not the climb
video_script.design: One idea: the rise is the top reading take away the bottom reading. The wrong idea is that the top reading is the rise. Punjab's line stays on screen all video; the lowest and highest dots light up in turn.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>The line goes up and down through the year. How far does it rise from its lowest month to its highest month?

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the rise is thirty eight degrees, because the line reaches thirty eight in June.
<bookmark mark='height'/>But thirty eight tells us the height of the dot, not how far the line climbed.
<bookmark mark='start'/>The climb also needs the height where the line started.
